spec.description: The metrics of the Temporal server, the engine, that Flowrensic reads from the metrics endpoint of the engine or that a worker forwards. The section shows how fast this data comes in, as items and as bytes per second, and how much of it is stored. The whole section has no data or stays at 0 when no env has an engine metrics address and no worker forwards engine metrics.

options.content:
## Engine
The engine's own metrics, scraped by the server or forwarded by a worker.

spec.title: Engine items per second
spec.description: Items of engine data stored per second, summed over all servers. An item is a sample, one number of the engine at one time. A refused request stores nothing and counts nothing. There is no good or bad value of its own: it follows how much your Temporal system does. Compare it with earlier days; a drop to 0 while your system works means this data stopped coming in. No data or a flat 0 when no env has an engine metrics address and no worker forwards engine metrics.

spec.title: Engine bytes per second
spec.description: Bytes of engine data stored per second, summed over all servers: the size of the answer of the engine, or of the request the worker sent. There is no good or bad value of its own. Read it with the items per second: more bytes for each item means larger items. No data or a flat 0 when no env has an engine metrics address and no worker forwards engine metrics.

spec.title: Engine stored size
spec.description: Size on disk of all engine data stored, in bytes: the engine_metrics table. One value for the whole install, so several servers on one database show the same size. Normal: it grows with use and levels off once retention deletes old data. Bad: it keeps growing; the storage against its size limit is on the sustainability dashboard. No data when the server could not read the size, which it logs as a warning.

The four panels show how many requests reach it, how fast they are answered, and how many were answered with ok or not. The whole section has no data when no worker runs the Flowrensic interceptor.

options.content:
## IngestActivityEvents
Activity attempts a worker interceptor sends.

spec.title: IngestActivityEvents requests per second
spec.description: Requests to IngestActivityEvents per second, summed over all servers, whatever the answer. There is no good or bad value of its own: it follows how much the senders send. A drop to 0 while they run means they stopped sending. No data until the first request, so it stays empty when no worker runs the Flowrensic interceptor.

spec.title: IngestActivityEvents response latency p95 second
spec.description: The time in seconds in which 95% of the requests to IngestActivityEvents were answered, over the last few minutes, all servers together. Normal: well under 1 second, the request time limit by default, which the sustainability dashboard draws for each kind of request. Bad: a line that climbs or stays high; senders may time out and send again. No data when there was no request in that time, so it stays empty when no worker runs the Flowrensic interceptor.

spec.title: IngestActivityEvents responses ok per second
spec.description: Requests to IngestActivityEvents answered with ok per second, summed over all servers. Normal: the same as all the requests. Bad: lower than all the requests; the panel on the right shows the others. No data until the first ok answer, so it stays empty when no worker runs the Flowrensic interceptor.

spec.title: IngestActivityEvents responses nok per second
spec.description: Requests to IngestActivityEvents answered with any code but ok per second, summed over all servers: refused as not valid, refused while the server sheds load, or failed. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, the sender did not get its data in; the warn and error lines on the platform dashboard and the Shedding row of the sustainability dashboard say why. No data until the first answer that is not ok, so an empty panel is the normal case.

The server lists the runs of each namespace of the engine and fetches the histories it does not hold yet. A poll is one pass over one namespace. A fetch is one history read from the engine. Each line is all namespaces and servers together. The whole section has no data when no namespace is set to be pulled.

options.content:
## Pull histories
The server lists the runs of each namespace and fetches the histories it does not hold.

spec.title: Polls per second
spec.description: Polls per second, whatever the result. Normal: steady, about one for each namespace in each poll interval. Bad: a drop to 0 while the engine runs, the puller stopped. No data before the first poll, so it stays empty when no namespace is set to be pulled.

spec.title: Poll duration p95
spec.description: The time in seconds in which 95% of the polls ended, over the last few minutes. Normal: well under the poll interval. Bad: close to the interval or above it; the puller falls behind, see its job section on the sustainability dashboard. No data when there was no poll in that time, so it stays empty when no namespace is set to be pulled.

spec.title: Poll failures per second
spec.description: Polls per second that ended with an error, for example when the engine could not be reached. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0; the warn and error lines of the server name the namespace and the error. No data before the first poll; from then on it shows 0, and it stays empty when no namespace is set to be pulled.

spec.title: History fetches per second
spec.description: Histories fetched from the engine per second. Normal: it follows how many runs start and change in the engine. Bad: 0 for a long time while runs change. No data before the first fetch, so it stays empty when no namespace is set to be pulled.

spec.title: Fetch duration p95
spec.description: The time in seconds in which 95% of the fetches of a history ended, over the last few minutes. Normal: well under a second for most histories; large histories take longer. Bad: a line that climbs; the engine is slow or the histories are large. No data when there was no fetch in that time, so it stays empty when no namespace is set to be pulled.

spec.title: Fetch failures per second
spec.description: Fetches per second that ended with an error. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, some histories were not stored and will be fetched again; the warn and error lines of the server say why. No data before the first fetch; from then on it shows 0, and it stays empty when no namespace is set to be pulled.

The server reads the metrics endpoint of each engine it knows the address of, a Temporal server you run or Temporal Cloud. A scrape is one read of one endpoint. Each line is all engines and servers together. The whole section has no data when no env has an engine metrics address.

options.content:
## Scrape engine metrics
The server reads the metrics endpoint of each engine it knows the address of.

spec.title: Scrapes per second
spec.description: Reads of an engine metrics endpoint per second, whatever the result. Normal: steady, one for each engine in each scrape interval. Bad: a drop to 0, the scraper stopped. No data before the first scrape, so it stays empty when no env has an engine metrics address.

spec.title: Scrape duration p95
spec.description: The time in seconds in which 95% of the scrapes ended, over the last few minutes. Normal: well under the scrape interval. Bad: close to the interval or above it; engine metrics come late. No data when there was no scrape in that time, so it stays empty when no env has an engine metrics address.

spec.title: Scrape failures per second
spec.description: Scrapes per second that ended with an error, for example when the endpoint could not be reached. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, engine metrics are missing; the warn lines of the server name the endpoint. No data before the first scrape; from then on it shows 0, and it stays empty when no env has an engine metrics address.

options.content:
## Scrape worker metrics
The server reads the customer's Prometheus endpoints that hold worker metrics, such as a collector's exporter, set in FLOWRENSIC_WORKER_SCRAPE_TARGETS.

spec.title: Worker scrapes per second
spec.description: Reads of a worker metrics endpoint per second, whatever the result. Normal: steady, one for each target in each scrape interval. Bad: a drop to 0, the scraper stopped. No data when FLOWRENSIC_WORKER_SCRAPE_TARGETS is not set.

spec.title: Worker scrape duration p95
spec.description: The time in seconds in which 95% of the scrapes of worker metrics ended, over the last few minutes. Normal: well under the scrape interval. Bad: close to the interval or above it. No data when FLOWRENSIC_WORKER_SCRAPE_TARGETS is not set, or when there was no scrape in that time.

spec.title: Worker scrape failures per second
spec.description: Scrapes of worker metrics per second that ended with an error, for example when the target could not be reached. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, worker metrics are missing; the warn lines of the server name the target. No data when FLOWRENSIC_WORKER_SCRAPE_TARGETS is not set; with a target set it shows 0 from the first try.

The endpoint IngestClientCalls takes in the calls of a Temporal client that threw, such as a query that failed, sent by the Flowrensic client interceptor. The four panels show how many requests reach it, how fast they are answered, and how many were answered with ok or not. The whole section has no data when no client runs the Flowrensic client interceptor.

options.content:
## IngestClientCalls
The queries a Temporal client made that threw, sent by the client interceptor.

spec.title: IngestClientCalls requests per second
spec.description: Requests to IngestClientCalls per second, summed over all servers, whatever the answer. There is no good or bad value of its own: it follows how much the senders send. A drop to 0 while they run means they stopped sending. No data until the first request, so it stays empty when no client runs the Flowrensic client interceptor.

spec.title: IngestClientCalls response latency p95 second
spec.description: The time in seconds in which 95% of the requests to IngestClientCalls were answered, over the last few minutes, all servers together. Normal: well under 1 second, the request time limit by default, which the sustainability dashboard draws for each kind of request. Bad: a line that climbs or stays high; senders may time out and send again. No data when there was no request in that time, so it stays empty when no client runs the Flowrensic client interceptor.

spec.title: IngestClientCalls responses ok per second
spec.description: Requests to IngestClientCalls answered with ok per second, summed over all servers. Normal: the same as all the requests. Bad: lower than all the requests; the panel on the right shows the others. No data until the first ok answer, so it stays empty when no client runs the Flowrensic client interceptor.

spec.title: IngestClientCalls responses nok per second
spec.description: Requests to IngestClientCalls answered with any code but ok per second, summed over all servers: refused as not valid, refused while the server sheds load, or failed. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, the sender did not get its data in; the warn and error lines on the platform dashboard and the Shedding row of the sustainability dashboard say why. No data until the first answer that is not ok, so an empty panel is the normal case.

What the buffer of each worker lost and holds, one line for each env. A worker running the Flowrensic interceptor keeps what it has to send in a buffer and sends it to the server in batches. An env is one Temporal environment of the Flowrensic config. Each panel shows 0 for every env of the config from the start, and the whole section has no data when the config has no env.

options.content:
## Worker sends
What the buffer of each worker lost and holds, by env: records it dropped, sends it gave up at their timeout, and records waiting to be sent.

spec.title: Records dropped per second
spec.description: Records per second that workers dropped from their buffer, by env: the buffer was full, or a send failed or timed out. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, data was lost, so findings may miss runs or attempts. No data only when the config has no env; each env shows 0 from the start.

spec.title: Sends timed out per second
spec.description: Sends per second that workers gave up at their timeout, by env. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, the server answers too slowly or cannot be reached; see the request time of the ingest endpoints above. No data only when the config has no env; each env shows 0 from the start.

spec.title: Records waiting to be sent
spec.description: Records waiting in the buffers of the workers of each env, a count, as each worker last reported. Normal: low, and back down after each send. Bad: a line that keeps growing; workers collect faster than they send, and records are dropped once the buffer is full. No data only when the config has no env; each env shows 0 from the start.

spec.title: Answers 429 per second
spec.description: Reads per second that Temporal Cloud refused with the answer 429, because its metrics endpoint allows only so many reads. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, some engine metrics are missing and findings about the engine may come late. No data when no env is on Temporal Cloud; an env on Temporal Cloud shows 0 from its first read.

spec.title: Cut answers per second
spec.description: Reads per second where Temporal Cloud sent only part of the metrics. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, some engine metrics are missing and findings about the engine may come late. No data when no env is on Temporal Cloud; an env on Temporal Cloud shows 0 from its first read.
